dimensions.rationale: All document types explicitly named across AK and AL statutes in the context of sealing/signing obligations or prohibitions were included as distinct items; synonyms and trivial variants (e.g., 'final drawings'/'drawings', 'shop drawings'/'field drawings') were merged, while genuinely different document types (e.g., plats vs. plans, calculations vs. reports) were kept separate; items appearing only in exclusion/prohibition clauses (e.g., shop drawings, instruments of service, affidavits) were retained as in-scope vocabulary items.

dimensions.rationale: The union was drawn by reading every sentence for any person, entity, or activity explicitly stated to be exempt from (or treated as not subject to) licensure requirements across all states; synonymous phrasings (e.g., 'engineer intern' / 'engineer-in-training') were merged into one entry, while genuinely distinct categories (e.g., agricultural work vs. revegetation, in-house corporate engineering vs. regulated utility engineering) were kept separate; items appearing only in prohibition/exclusion lists were included because they identify in-scope exemption categories a state happens to restrict.

dimensions.rationale: Only Alaska's statute explicitly names required engineering disciplines for board composition; civil, electrical, mechanical, mining, petroleum, chemical, and a catch-all 'other branch' seat are enumerated — petroleum and chemical appear as alternates to the mining seat but are still statutorily named disciplines, so each is kept as a distinct entry; 'electrical or mechanical' is split into separate canonical entries since the statute treats them as distinct disciplines that may each independently occupy a seat.
